blocks.title: Billions of Switches on a Fingernail
blocks.subtitle: How integrated circuits are designed, verified and manufactured

blocks.text:
A modern processor holds billions of transistors, each a switch far smaller than a virus, wired together by kilometres of metal thinner than a wavelength of light. Very-large-scale integration (VLSI) is the engineering that makes such a thing possible, and makes it work the first time.

No person can place a billion transistors by hand. The story of VLSI is largely the story of automation and abstraction.

blocks.heading: Abstraction makes it manageable
blocks.text: Designers describe behaviour in a hardware description language at **register-transfer level**. Tools then translate that description into logic gates, place the gates on the chip, route the wires between them and check that timing, power and manufacturing rules are all met. Each level hides the detail of the one beneath.

steps.text: **Describe.** Engineers write RTL in Verilog or VHDL and simulate it against tests until its behaviour is correct.
**Synthesise.** A synthesis tool maps the RTL onto a library of standard cells such as gates and flip-flops.
**Place and route.** Cells are positioned on the die and connected through many metal layers, with clocks and power distributed across the chip.
**Sign off and fabricate.** Timing, power and design rules are verified. The layout goes to the foundry, where it is printed layer by layer.

blocks.heading: Why CMOS won
blocks.text: Complementary MOS logic pairs an n-type and a p-type transistor so that, in a steady state, one of them is always off. Almost no current flows except while switching. That low static power is what allowed millions, then billions, of gates on one chip without melting it. As transistors shrank, leakage returned as a major concern and drove new structures such as FinFETs.

items.title: CMOS
items.text: Logic built from complementary n- and p-type transistors; the basis of nearly all digital chips.

items.title: Moore's law
items.text: Gordon Moore's 1965 observation that transistor counts on a chip double at a regular interval.

items.title: FinFET
items.text: A transistor whose channel is a raised fin wrapped by the gate, giving better control and less leakage.

items.title: Photolithography
items.text: Projecting a pattern through a mask onto light-sensitive resist to define each layer.

items.title: Standard cell
items.text: A pre-designed, pre-characterised gate or flip-flop used as a building block.

items.title: Timing closure
items.text: Making every signal path fast enough for the target clock, and not too fast for hold requirements.

blocks.heading: Life after easy scaling
blocks.text: Shrinking transistors no longer makes them faster and cooler for free. Leakage, heat density, lithography cost and atomic-scale variation all push back. Progress now comes from new transistor structures, extreme-ultraviolet lithography, stacking chips in three dimensions and designing processors specialised for particular workloads.

items.title: Processors
items.text: CPUs and GPUs for computers, phones and data centres.

items.title: Communications
items.text: Radio transceivers and baseband chips in every handset and base station.

items.title: Automotive and aerospace
items.text: Controllers qualified for wide temperatures and long life.

blocks.question: Why does static CMOS logic draw very little power when idle?
options: In a steady state one transistor of each complementary pair is off
blocks.explanation: With either the pull-up or the pull-down network off, there is no direct path from supply to ground.

blocks.question: What does logic synthesis produce?
options: A gate-level netlist from an RTL description
blocks.explanation: Synthesis maps the behavioural description onto cells from a library.

blocks.heading: Key terms and next steps
blocks.text:
**RTL**: register-transfer level description. **Netlist**: a list of components and their connections. **Die**: one chip on a wafer. **Yield**: the fraction of dice that work. **EDA**: electronic design automation software.
